problems_found.problem: H1 'Revenue is slowing. Costs are rising. Your team is waiting for a decision. Which problem do you solve first?' is 19 words, well over the spec's 9-word cap (section 8, governance checklist item 1). The writer's hand-back flagged this as intentional because it follows the spec's own verbatim example for this page (section 8). But section 8's per-page examples and the governance checklist's numeric cap are in tension, and the checklist is the operative rule a reviewer runs (section 12, item 1) — a spec example is not exempt from the checklist it sits above. Checked whether a shorter H1 keeps the meaning: the dropped clause ('Your team is waiting for a decision') is already carried by the lede ('while the people who must act on it wait'), so nothing is lost by cutting it from the H1.
problems_found.fix: Shortened H1 to 'Revenue slows, costs rise. Which do you solve first?' (9 words). Keeps both pressures, the question form, and 'solve first' near-verbatim from the original; the team-waiting clause remains in the lede immediately below.

notes: Everything else on the page checked clean: narrative-spine SPINE array matches the from-carrying-to-leading structure without naming outcomes; CERTIFICATE_POSITIONING.distinction and .professionalRelevance render together in the same block (line ~201) wherever the certificate/CMI/assessment is named; assessment is stated presence-first ('Assessment is the written action plan reviewed by faculty; there is no traditional thesis or examination.'); servant leadership named exactly once on the page beside FLOW, worded 'measured by the people it serves' (not 'most'), matching the owner's banned-word constraint; no retyped facts (FACTS.durationLong/trainingDays/liveSessions tokens used throughout); no ladder/rung/climb language; CtaSection heading names the reader's own decision.
